sources.entry: Funky - Easily toggle the function key on your Mac on a per app basis.

summary.one_liner: Funky is a macOS status bar utility that toggles whether the function keys act as standard F1, F2, etc. on a per-app basis.
summary.what_it_does: Funky runs in the Mac status bar and keeps a list of apps for which the function keys are set to standard F1, F2, and so on. You manage that list from the Preferences dialog under Apps, using the plus sign to add an app bundle. The README describes the app as a per-app toggle and does not list other features. Bug reports and feature requests go through the GitHub issue tracker. Pre-built binaries are available from GitHub Releases and the Mac App Store.
use_cases: Use F1-F12 keys as standard function keys in specific apps
Toggle function key behavior per application on macOS
Keep media key behavior default while using F-keys in one app
Install a status bar utility for function key control on a Mac
how_to_run: Download a pre-built binary from the GitHub Releases section or the Mac App Store
Click the status bar icon and open Preferences
Go to the Apps section and use the + sign to add an app bundle
To build from source, set the DEVELOPMENT variable to 1 in main.m or pass it as a compile-time define to skip the Mac App Store receipt check
notable: Per-app function key behavior, set from a status bar menu
Available as a free download from the Mac App Store and as GitHub release binaries
Build option to skip the Mac App Store receipt validation during development
caveats: Release builds fail to start without a Mac App Store receipt unless the DEVELOPMENT flag is set to 1
The author states limited time for maintenance and invites outside contributions
keywords: use f keys in one app
make f1 work in an app
